about: Running bug log. One object per bug; keep fixed bugs for reference. List open bugs: jq '.bugs[] | select(.fixed == false) | {id, title}' bugs_to_fix.json

bugs.title: Chart throws "Value is null" when reloading after a strategy switch
bugs.found_by: Strengthened dashboard browser test (tests/dashboard_ui_smoke.mjs) failed with 'Browser errors: Value is null'.
bugs.symptom: Browser console logged 'Uncaught Error: Value is null' one to three times. The chart still ended up drawn correctly, so users couldn't see it. It failed the browser test, which treats any browser error as a failure.
reproduce: Start the dashboard: ./start.command (or uv run python src/tradingview_mcp/ui/server.py).
Open it in Chrome with DevTools → Console open.
Click the Advanced tab. Pick resolution 12H and range 5Y.
Change the strategy dropdown to Bollinger, then back to Sloped Lines (this loads saved best parameters and resets the chart to 1D / 1Y).
Trigger any reload of the chart: click range 5Y, or the Regular tab.
'Value is null' appears in the console shortly after the reload.
bugs.reproduce_automated: npm run test:ui — its final step (click 5Y right after switching back to Sloped Lines) is this sequence and now guards against regression. Waiting before the click did not avoid the bug; it is not a click-timing issue.
bugs.cause: The main chart shares one time scale across the candles and every overlay line. updateDashboard() loaded the new candles first and removed the previous trendline/channel overlay series only later, after the new trendlines were fetched. Removing series after the swap shifted the shared time-scale positions under the new candles, so the library looked up bars at positions that no longer existed.
stack_traces: Error: Value is null at ensureNotNull ← TimeScale._internal_timeRangeForLogicalRange ← TimeScaleApi.getVisibleRange ← TimeScaleApi._private__onVisibleBarsChanged (visible-time-range event)
Error: Value is null at ensureNotNull ← SeriesBarColorer.Candlestick ← SeriesCandlesticksPaneView._internal__createRawItem (drawing a candle)
bugs.debug_tip: For readable stack traces, temporarily replace the bundled library with https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/lightweight-charts@4.1.3/dist/lightweight-charts.standalone.development.js
dead_ends: Switching the listener from subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange to subscribeVisibleLogicalRangeChange removed the first trace but not the second. Not needed once the real cause was fixed; reverted.
Waiting (animation frames + 500 ms, up to 3 s) before the next click did not avoid the error.
bugs.fix: In updateDashboard(), remove the old trendline and channel overlay series before candlestickSeries.setData(...). New overlays are still added after the new candles. Side effect: during a reload the old lines vanish right away instead of staying until the new ones arrive.
bugs.verified: npm run test:ui passed 3/3 runs; 38/38 Python tests pass. On the Advanced tab, dragging and zooming the main chart still keeps the volume and RSI panels aligned (Playwright check, no browser errors).

bugs.title: Sloped trendlines can reactivate after crossing through price
bugs.found_by: AAPL 1Y / 1D chart review showed the descending resistance anchored on December 3 and December 26 crossing candle bodies before its January 27 breakout.
bugs.symptom: A trendline could visibly cut through one or more later candles, disappear as a valid candidate, then be selected again after price moved back to the other side. The chart also labeled the second anchor as the confirmation date even though a pivot becomes knowable only after the lookback bars complete.
reproduce: Open AAPL with the saved Sloped Lines configuration at 1D / 1Y.
Inspect the descending resistance beginning December 3, 2025 and anchored again December 26, 2025.
Observe candle bodies crossing the projected line after the second anchor before the line ends on January 27, 2026.
bugs.cause: Candidate validation checked candles only between the two anchors plus the current evaluation candle. It skipped every candle after anchor two and before the current candle, allowing an invalidated candidate to become valid again later. Swing points also discarded their actual confirmation bar, and the UI redrew only endpoint interpolation instead of the strategy's per-bar projection.
bugs.fix: Preserve each swing's actual confirmation bar; validate every candle from anchor one through the current bar; permit formation tolerance only before anchor two; invalidate on any selected body or wick touch after anchor two; use inclusive active-line breaks; and send one projected trendline value per candle to the UI.
bugs.verified: The former December 3 → December 26 → January 27 line no longer appears. AAPL now draws a clear December 3 → April 23 resistance, activates it after the April 30 pivot confirmation, and ends it May 1. 42 Python tests pass and the 19-case dashboard browser matrix passes across Regular/Advanced, 1D/4H/12H, and 3M/1Y/5Y.
bugs.performance_impact: For AAPL's saved 1Y / 1D parameters on data from 2025-09-26 through 2026-09-25, the corrected engine returns 15.83% across 4 trades with a 50.0% win rate. The stored 46.71% badge remains a historical baseline from the previous engine and requires re-optimization before replacement.

bugs.title: SPY Saved Best omits historical date window and line validation settings
bugs.symptom: Saved Best displays the historical 17.07% label while the current SPY run returns 7.73% across only two trades.
reproduce: Click Saved Best and compare the P&L with the saved historical return.
bugs.cause: The legacy preset has no captured dates, anchor_source or trendline_tolerance. Current defaults use confirmed pivots and zero tolerance, whereas the original engine used candidate candles and 1.5% tolerance with close validation. The original return was recorded on an older one-year window.
bugs.fix: Recorded the SPY historical daily window (2025-09-23 through 2026-09-22) and explicit any-valid-candle anchors, close validation, 1.5% tolerance, pivot lookback and disabled recovery/gap defaults. Preserved historical 17.07% metadata and recorded current-price verification at 17.06%.
bugs.verified: 52 Python tests pass. The original strategy implementation and current engine both return 17.06% across 11 trades at 72.7% win rate on current historical prices. Live Saved Best browser check restores the dates and settings and returns 17.06%.

bugs.title: Changing ticker automatically overwrites active strategy controls with saved parameters
bugs.symptom: Switching AAPL to SPY clears an enabled Close > 5-Bar High recovery checkbox without clicking Saved Best.
reproduce: Enable Recovery Re-entry Any and Close > 5-Bar High on AAPL.
Select SPY without clicking Saved Best.
Observe recovery settings reset to the SPY preset.
bugs.cause: Ticker changes call applyBestParametersIfAvailable, which applies saved controls, resolution and range while fetching the preset badge.
bugs.fix: Only explicit Saved Best clicks apply controls, resolution, range and captured dates. Ticker changes fetch badge metadata without overwriting controls, and rebind the retained fixed date window to the new symbol. Yahoo chart symbol changes retain their selected window too.
bugs.verified: Dashboard browser checks retain every Sloped Lines input, resolution, range, session and dates across AAPL, SPY and a symbol with no preset. Explicit Saved Best clicks still replace them. Charts smoke test passes; a live AAPL-to-SPY check confirms recovery remains enabled until SPY Saved Best is clicked.

bugs.title: Yahoo data failures cause empty charts and repeated slow requests
bugs.symptom: The dashboard page responds immediately, but an AAPL daily candle request takes about 10.9 seconds and returns an empty candle array; the graph appears stalled.
reproduce: Open the dashboard and request AAPL 1Y daily candles while Yahoo requests are failing.
Observe repeated no-price-data messages and empty chart data.
Probe Yahoo public chart endpoint; it currently responds HTTP 429.
bugs.cause: Yahoo is refusing the direct chart probe with HTTP 429. The app returns empty candles on failed Yahoo history requests and only caches successful results, so candles, trades, statistics and trendlines can repeatedly fetch the failing provider. Several async request handlers execute synchronous fetch/calculation work directly, delaying unrelated page requests.
bugs.verified: 99 offline Python tests, 8 JavaScript unit tests, charts build/lint, React chart browser smoke and dashboard window/settings smoke passed. Reconstructed local AAPL Saved Best snapshot reproduces 49.01%; SPY reproduces 17.06% while its original 17.07% record remains unchanged. Verified cached prices remain readable after provider failures and process-store restart, and a slow provider does not block dashboard HTML. Live restarted-server check: AAPL 250 cached daily candles in 0.011 seconds; initial Hyperliquid BTC minute history persisted 2562 candles in 1.0117 seconds and repeat request took 0.0454 seconds.
bugs.diagnostic_before_fix: Dashboard HTML returned HTTP 200 in 0.001247 seconds. AAPL daily candle request returned HTTP 200 after 10.921413 seconds with zero candles. A page request during the fetch took 2.724866 seconds. A direct Yahoo chart API probe returned HTTP 429 in 0.180546 seconds. Server process remained listening on port 8000 with low CPU usage.
bugs.fix: Persist shared Yahoo/Hyperliquid historical candles and coverage in SQLite; coalesce downloads using durable leases and provider cooldowns; serve cached history while refreshing off the ASGI event loop; return explicit errors for failed/incomplete backtests; pin chart calculations to immutable revisions and Saved Best snapshots.

bugs.title: Saved Best snapshot binding survives ticker and resolution changes
bugs.symptom: Switching from AAPL Saved Best to SPY retains the AAPL snapshot ID and receives HTTP 422; changing resolution/session can likewise attach an incompatible snapshot.
bugs.cause: The existing ticker handler copies captured dates to the new ticker without removing the newly introduced snapshot ID. Captured-window query construction does not distinguish chart resolution or session.
bugs.verified: Dashboard settings/window smoke and React chart smoke pass with snapshot IDs. Regression checks cover ticker switching, alternate resolutions, sessions and data sources; 99 Python and 9 JavaScript unit tests pass.
bugs.fix: Clear snapshot binding on ticker changes while retaining active controls and captured dates. Attach IDs only for matching captured resolutions/sessions on both chart pages; VIX requests omit the main ticker snapshot.

bugs.title: Dashboard favicon request produces a browser console error
bugs.symptom: Opening the live dashboard produces GET /favicon.ico HTTP 404 and a browser console error.
bugs.cause: There is no favicon route or linked icon.
bugs.verified: New route is present in the tested app; final live Chrome check verifies no console errors.
bugs.fix: Return HTTP 204 from the favicon route instead of an unhandled HTTP 404.
